basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Et vocavit Adam nomen uxoris suae Eva, eo quod mater esset cunctorum viventium. Et hoc'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Et vocavit Adam nomen uxoris suae Eva, eo quod mater esset cunctorum viventium. Et hoc nomen Adam divino instinctu constat uxori suae posuisse, quod aptissime congruit Ecclesiae sanctae, in cujus solum unitate, quae catholica vocatur, vitae cunctis janua patet.
